A chance decision to take an alternative route on an otherwise ordinary day in 2020 led Italy-based businessman Sukhdev Singh Kang to Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi’s ancestral home in Lusiana, Italy, which he eventually acquired.
But Kang has ambitions beyond simply owning the house. He wants to preserve its legacy and hopes to turn it into a museum. “Through your medium, we are reaching out to the Gandhi family. If they can guide us on how to convert the house into a museum, it would be wonderful,” Kang tells Mayank Kumar in an exclusive interview for ThePrint.
